key_insight: RASP separates reading from learning: inference uses every LoRA atom, while training updates only a sparse subset within one fixed-size adapter.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support memory-constrained continual adaptation of engineering vision systems, but the abstract does not demonstrate constitutive modeling or solid-mechanics applications.
method: A scene-modulated cosine router selects the top-q unlocked atoms for gradient updates while retaining all atoms for inference.
A Gram-coherence penalty discourages overlap between active and non-updated output directions.
Activation traces and atom spectral norms guide Cauchy step attenuation and boundary anchor locking to consolidate knowledge.
evidence_signal: Across CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A, the abstract reports matching or surpassing branch-expanding LoRA learners with a constant adapter parameter footprint.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical results or routing-cost measurements, so accuracy gains and runtime overhead require verification.
paper_title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
